sources.title: On Artificial Viewers, Followers, and Chat Activity
sources.access: Search-service text extraction of official page; no original HTTP headers/body retained.
sources.locator: Main article, paragraphs on fake chat, harassment and responses.
sources.summary: Twitch acknowledged artificial chat activity and bot-enabled harassment, alongside commercial engagement manipulation. It described technical detection, staff investigations and legal action.
limitations: Historical platform statement, not another incident measurement.
No attribution to Russia; described safeguards do not establish their effectiveness in a particular stream.

sources.title: Kremlin Playbook Spotlight: A Washington Think-Tank Event and a Russian Troll
sources.publisher: CSIS; Heather A. Conley and Holly Geffs
sources.observation_date_as_reported: 2018-06-25; stated in source excerpt, not independently checked against event archive
sources.access: Substantial indexed text returned by targeted search. Direct page open returned HTTP 403; no VOD/chat archive inspected.
sources.locator: Opening incident description and attribution discussion.
sources.summary: CSIS described disruptive messages during its own YouTube event and assessed the account as likely a Russian troll. The article acknowledged difficulty establishing the origin of such accounts.
limitations: Source-assessed attribution, not proof of automation, state sponsorship or a coordinated network.
Historical event date is source-reported; no independent event-date validation.
This retains the publisher's attribution assessment; no independent factual replication was performed.

sources.title: Justice Department Leads Efforts Among Federal, International, and Private Sector Partners to Disrupt Covert Russian Government-Operated Social Media Bot Farm
sources.observation_period_as_reported: Posts from October-November 2023; disruption announced July 9, 2024
sources.access: Search-service text extraction of official release; underlying affidavits not independently reviewed in this pass.
sources.locator: Opening, Overview, and closing platform-response paragraphs.
sources.summary: DOJ attributed an AI-enabled X bot farm to RT/FSB-linked operators, citing warrant affidavits, and reported two domain seizures, searches involving 968 accounts and account suspensions by X.
limitations: Government investigative attribution; no adjudication claimed here.
X account activity, not evidence about Twitch or YouTube live chats.
Suspension is a reported intervention; prevention of harm and durable recovery are unmeasured here.

sources.title: Operation Overload's underwhelming influence and evolving tactics
sources.access: Search-service text extraction of original research report; underlying sample not independently replicated.
sources.locator: Key findings, Methodology, and Minor modifications, insignificant impact.
sources.summary: ISD reported removal of 73% of sampled X posts and over 90% on TikTok and Bluesky. Analysts found little organic engagement in remaining material and reported no detected bot activity on Bluesky.
limitations: Attributed research findings for a bounded sample; removal is not proof that all exposure or harm was prevented.
No causal estimate of persuasion and no complete census.
Separate campaign/sample; not confirmation of the CSIS incident.
